newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi stocks tend firmer, volumes subdued.
newsitem.headline: Saudi stocks tend firmer, volumes subdued.

text.p: Shares on Saudi Arabia's stock exchange ended the week to Thursday 0.73 perecnt higher, but trading was subdued and focused mainly on bank shares, the Riyadh-based Bakheet Financial Advisors (BFA) said on Saturday.
The all-share index closed up at 162.46 points from 161.28 points the previous week.
A total of 1.48 million shares were traded in the week, down from 2.9 million shares a week earlier.
Banking sector shares accounted for 46 percent of total trading value which BFA put at 342.6 million riyals ($91 million), 41 percent lower than the previous week's 585 million riyals.
BFA attributed the sharp drop in volumes to the start of summer holidays.
Of the 58 shares traded in the week, 28 rose, eight dropped and 22 were unchanged.

Al-Ahsa Development led market gainers with a 5.1 percent increase to 104 riyals from a previous 99 riyals. United Saudi Commercial Bank closed 4.7 percent higher at 334 riyals from 319 a week earlier.
Al-Mawashi al-Mukairish closed at 90 riyals down from 92 riyals and NADEC at 106 riyals from 108 riyals.
